title: Internal control-plane REST API contract (M1 single tenant)
source_of_truth: docs/adr/sandbox-lifecycle.md section 3 (Proposed, 2026-09-22): unified /v1 API — endpoint names, state/operation semantics are normative here
docs/adr/usage-ledger.md section 1 (Proposed): operation_id / generation / ledger_seq event envelope the API fronts
docs/contracts/runner-lifecycle.json: state machine and refusals the API fronts; verified by scripts/verify_runner_contract.py
docs/contracts/cli-surface.json: exit codes the CLI maps from these API errors
docs/contracts/terminal-protocol.json: hello frame the terminal ticket is presented at
issue #76: [T09] M1 internal control-plane minimal API

executable_double.nature: stdlib-only in-memory test double; request(method, path, headers, body) -> (status, json); snapshot()/restore() simulates API restart; no HTTP server, no external deps

implementation_status.real_backend: not started: TypeScript + Hono + Postgres per the language decision; blocked on #11 runner (which waits on the #8 GO)

auth.binding: API listens on loopback or an SSH tunnel (or an otherwise verified trusted channel) only; the Runner management interface is reachable only from the control plane

endpoints.purpose: create a sandbox (only agent=claude in M1)

body.runtime_deadline_at: optional UTC epoch ms or null (no default runtime limit)

responses.when: admission (milliCPU, memory, volume) rejects; no operation, no sandbox

endpoints.state_effect: sandbox enters observed_state=Creating with desired_state=Active, generation=1; observed becomes Active only when the create operation is confirmed by Runner evidence

endpoints.purpose: list sandboxes (CLI ls / Web); Destroyed tombstones are not listed
inspect one sandbox (tombstone still queryable after Destroyed)

responses.body: desired_state, observed_state, generation, version, pending_operation, last_confirmed_at, volumes, runtime_deadline_at, session (null when unrecorded); Error adds last_confirmed_state and error{code, resources[]}; Active/Idle add hold and next_transition_at (null when no countdown)

responses.when: unknown id — same answer for forged and cross-scope ids, no probe signal

endpoints.purpose: request a state change (Active | Idle | Suspend) via an operation; there is no separate /idle /suspend /resume endpoint (ADR section 3)

body.expected_version: integer, must equal the sandbox version
body.credential: optional secret re-sent by the CLI for resume; excluded from Idempotency-Key body comparison, never stored, logged, or echoed in the operation payload

responses.when: same target already synchronously achieved and nothing pending — no second transition
Suspend->Active (or Error/Lost retry) without a credential; no operation created, stays Suspend

another change is pending, an opposite operation arrives while Suspending, any change while Resuming/Creating/Destroying, state change on Destroyed, or action on Error/Lost before reconciliation/fencing, or an operation undefined for the current state (refuse-on-unknown)
state enum or expected_version missing/wrong, or Idempotency-Key header absent

endpoints.state_effect: accept moves observed into the acceptance-driven intermediate state only (Suspending / Resuming, per the runner contract transitions); resume from Suspend/Error/Lost allocates a new generation; Idle/Active policy switches keep the previous observed_state with a pending operation until confirmed

endpoints.purpose: destroy: removes processes and first-version workspace/home volumes after explicit scope confirmation

body.expected_version: integer, must equal the sandbox version
body.confirm_scope: must be the literal 'workspace_and_home_volumes' (explicit data-deletion scope)

responses.when: destroy while Suspending/Resuming (no contract transition), or on Error/Lost before reconciliation, or a state change on Destroyed
expected_version or confirm_scope missing/wrong, or Idempotency-Key absent

endpoints.state_effect: accept moves observed to Destroying; repeating destroy after Destroyed returns the existing operation, never a second one (destroyed_is_terminal)

endpoints.purpose: poll an operation to its terminal state

mint the short-lived attach credential presented in the terminal protocol hello frame (token field, #12); the attach-time state gate (sandbox_not_active, wrong_generation) belongs to the terminal protocol (#13), not this REST edge

responses.when: unknown or destroyed sandbox (same answer as terminal reconnect_after_destroy)

endpoints.state_effect: none; tickets are single-purpose, expire, and are invalidated by an API restart

endpoints.note: workspace policy with expected_version, audit trail and effective time; owned by the workspace-policy track, not this slice
{runtime_deadline_at: UTC|null, expected_version}, 200 with the new value plus audit; not exercised by this slice's tests

fields.operation_id: opaque id, referenced by usage-ledger events as operation_id
fields.target: requested change; never contains the credential
fields.expected_version: fencing version the request carried (null for create)
fields.generation: generation in effect for the operation; resume allocates a new one
fields.retryable: bool; true for failed operations after the client re-reads state

semantics: every state-change/destroy request answers 202 with the operation; clients poll GET /v1/operations/{id} until succeeded/failed
at most one change operation per sandbox at a time; conflicts answer 409
a request timeout does NOT imply not-executed: the client must poll the operation; unknown outcome resolves to Lost via lease expiry, never to an assumption

idempotency.scope: per token/tenant and operation scope; one key maps to at most one accepted request
idempotency.same_key_same_body: the original operation is returned again (no double-create, no second transition); replays stay answerable after an API restart because the map is persisted
idempotency.credential_rule: the credential field never participates in the body comparison (ADR section 3)

runtime_honesty.rule: observed_state is set only from confirmed Runner observation; desired_state alone changes nothing; HTTP 202 is acceptance, not success
runtime_honesty.unknown_outcome: unconfirmed creates stay observed Creating (pending); lease expiry moves the sandbox to Lost — never an optimistic Active
sources: docs/adr/usage-ledger.md section 1: accepted request != runtime applied; only confirmed observation switches resource intervals

security.single_tenant_m1: exactly one workspace; forged workspace/sandbox ids stay inside internal scope — unknown ids answer 404 with no cross-tenant probe signal (multi-tenant authorization is #16)
security.secrets: credentials are never persisted in the general DB, never logged, never echoed in operation payloads or snapshots; the double stores only a has_credential boolean

state_machine.source: docs/contracts/runner-lifecycle.json (loaded, not duplicated, by the double)
state_machine.rule: transitions outside the table are refused (refuse-on-unknown); no /idle /suspend /resume endpoints exist

capacity_admission.divergence_note: runner-lifecycle.json records http_status 409 for the runner-side capacity-exceeded refusal; this API edge maps admission rejection to 429 per the #76 slice instruction. Reconcile the two layers when the real backend lands (#11).

errors.when: Idempotency-Key replayed with a different body
pending conflict, opposite/unknown operation for the state, pre-reconciliation Error/Lost, terminal Destroyed

error_model.cli_exit_note: interim mapping for #14 (cli-surface.json owns the exit codes); 2xx maps to 0

related_tickets.role: owner: this API slice; part 1 contract/test-double, part 2 real Go-runner integration blocked on #11
